content: Veronica officinalis, also known as Heath Speedwell, Common Speedwell, Common Gypsyweed, or Paul's Betony, is a species of the Veronica genus. It is native to Europe and western Asia. This plant is also commonly referred to as Common Speedwell and Common Gypsyweed. It is a herbaceous perennial plant characterized by hairy green stems that grow to a length of 10 to 50 cm. These stems spread across the ground in mats and produce short vertical shoots that bear delicate violet flowers. The leaves of the plant are 5 to 5 cm long, 1 to 3 cm wide, and softly hairy. This species of speedwell thrives in fields and areas that have been disturbed. It has the potential to become a weed if its seeds contaminate agricultural seed collections, such as alfalfa. Historically, the green parts of the plant have been used medicinally to treat conditions such as coughs, otitis media (middle ear infections), and gastrointestinal distress. The plant is rich in vitamins, tannins, and a glycoside known as aucuboside. Aucuboside, which is also present in many other species of the Plantaginaceae family, is believed to possess anti-inflammatory properties. Extracts of Veronica officinalis are widely marketed as herbal remedies for sinus and ear infections. This plant has been introduced to North America, where it has become widely naturalized.
